events.text: Payment Order Initiation SD
1. What Is This Service Domain?
In BIAN v14.0, the Payment Order Initiation Service Domain manages the capture, registration, and initiation of customer payment orders across all banking channels.

Role: It acts as the primary entry-point Processing Domain that receives a payment instruction from a channel or orchestration layer, enriches it with system-controlled attributes, and creates a traceable instance record of that payment order.

Classification: This is a Transaction / Processing Domain — not a Catalog or Directory Domain. It processes and registers payment instructions; it does not manage product definitions, account state, or party profiles.
1.1 Key Distinction

rows: Payment Order Initiation SD Does NOT Manage
Capture and registration of payment instructions
Creation of Payment Order Instance Records
Account balance management (Savings / Current Account SDs)
Party or account master data management
Payment instruction enrichment with system-controlled attributes
Traceability via Instance Reference and Transaction ID
Transaction history or ledger records (Position Keeping SD)
Behavior Qualifier sub-records — none at Initiation step

events.text: 1.2 Payment Order Types
A payment order processed by this SD may represent:

rows: Retail / Consumer transfer between two customer accounts
Customer payment towards a bill or obligation
Standard batch-settled credit transfer via ACH network
Bank operator processes payment on behalf of walk-in customer

events.text: 2. When to Use This Service Domain
Invoke this SD whenever a channel or system submits a new payment instruction for registration and downstream processing:

rows: Customer initiates transfer via mobile / internet banking
Channel collects payer, payee, amount, currency, datetime and submits to Initiate endpoint
Bank teller initiates payment on behalf of customer
Bank system submits customer payment details; channel enriches payload and calls Initiate
Bank funds customer account from internal account
Internal account used as payer; customer account used as payee; Initiate called by orchestration layer
Self transfer between customer's own accounts
Customer's two own accounts used as payer and payee; same Initiate endpoint used

events.text: 2.1 Use Case A — Customer-Initiated Fund Transfer (Mobile Banking)
Scenario: A retail customer initiates a transfer via the mobile banking app.

Action: The mobile app collects payer, payee, amount, currency, and payment datetime. The channel enriches the payload with pre-configured fields (DateTimeType = CreatingDate; PaymentMechanism = Book Transfer) and calls POST /PaymentOrderInitiation/Initiate.
Response: Unique Payment Instance Reference (e.g., POI-2026-00041823) and Payment Instance Status = Initiated.
2.2 Use Case B — Bank Operator-Initiated Payment
Scenario: A bank operator processes a payment instruction on behalf of a walk-in customer.

Action: The bank system submits the customer's payment details. The channel enriches the payload with pre-configured fields and calls the BIAN Initiate endpoint. The payment is registered and a unique Instance Reference is returned.
3. Implementation Scope

rows: Transfer between two different customers at the same bank
Out of scope — planned for future implementation
Customer transfers between their own accounts
Current scope — implemented in demo flow
Bank funds customer account from bank's internal account
Current scope — implemented in demo flow

events.text: 4. Level of Detail to Capture
Data captured must meet the following quality requirements:

rows: All fields relate to a single, specific payment instruction event
Not account-level or party-level data — captures the transfer instruction only
Every payment order receives a unique Payment Order Reference (e.g., POI-2026-00041823)
Only the fields required to register and post the instruction are captured; no BQ sub-records at this stage

events.text: 5. Control Record Structure
All payment order fields are captured within the CR payload. There are no BQ sub-records at the Initiation step. The CR groups fields into the following logical areas:

rows: FinancialTransactionFromAccount — AccountIdentification (account number, account type enum)
FinancialTransactionTargetAccount — AccountIdentification (account number, account type enum)
Amount (AmountValue), Currency (Currencycode), DateTime (DateTimeContent, DateTimeType = CreatingDate), Mechanism (Book Transfer)

events.text: Response ID rule: PaymentTransactionIdentification[0] = TransactionID (CBS UUID); PaymentTransactionIdentification[1] = PaymentOrderID (adapter-generated, same as Client Batch ID submitted to CBS).
6. Payment Workflow — Current Scope
6.1 Use Case 2 — Self Transfer (Customer's Own Accounts)

The customer transfers funds between two accounts they own. The payer account and payee account both belong to the same customer. The adapter generates a unique Payment Order ID, submits a Book Transfer posting instruction to CBS, and returns the Payment Order Reference and Transaction ID.
6.2 Use Case 3 — Funding from Bank's Internal Account
The bank funds a customer account from an internal bank account. The payer is the bank's internal account; the payee is the customer account. The same Initiate endpoint and field mapping apply.
6.3 Use Case 1 — Intrabank Transfer (Out of Scope)
Transfer between two different customers at the same bank. This use case is planned for future implementation and is not part of the current demo scope.
7. Related Service Domains & Systems

rows: Transaction ID (CBS UUID) returned by Payment Order Initiation is reflected as Transaction ID in Position Keeping SD transaction logs.
Savings Account SD / Current Account SD
Account numbers referenced as payer and payee. Balance management is handled by respective account SDs — Payment Order Initiation does not manage account state.
Payer and payee names are optional reference fields. Authoritative party data remains in PRDD.
Receives the posting instruction from the adapter. Returns Posting Instruction Batch UUID (Transaction ID). CBS performs the actual account posting.
Not integrated in current demo scope. Will be the downstream routing engine for ACH, RTP, FedNow, SWIFT, and SEPA mechanisms in future phases.
